Need the patient's complete hepatobiliary enzyme profile including ALP, GGT, and bilirubin, along with right upper quadrant ultrasound or MRCP to assess bile duct structure and exclude obstruction, and if indicated antimitochondrial antibody testing or liver biopsy, as these are core examinations for confirming or ruling out biliary/cholestatic disease.
records.text:
- Laboratory Tests:
    * Aspartate aminotransferase: 55 U/L (reference: 13-30 U/L)
    * Alanine aminotransferase: 33 U/L (reference: 7-23 U/L)
    * Lactate dehydrogenase: 326 U/L (reference: 124-222 U/L)
    * Gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase: 257 U/L (reference: 9-32 U/L)
    * Alkaline phosphatase: 1028 U/L (reference: 106-322 U/L)
- Imaging Studies:
    * Abdominal Ultrasonography
      Title: Ultrasonographic findings of hepatic parenchyma
      Description: Coarse and heterogeneous relatively hyperechoic hepatic parenchyma as a whole and an irregular isoechoic region from the hepatic hilum to the right dorsal side
    * Gadolinium-enhanced MRI
      Title: MRI findings in hepatobiliary phase
      Description: Region corresponding to relatively hyperechoic hepatic parenchyma was clearly hypointense compared with hyperintensity in the region corresponding to the isoechoic region
- Pathological Findings:
    * Liver Biopsy (hyperechoic parenchyma):
      - Scattered clusters of malignant cells positive for PAX8
      - Malignant cells in Glisson's capsule, occluding interlobular vein
      - Inflammatory cells infiltrated into portal canal with destroyed interlobular bile ducts
    * Liver Biopsy (isoechoic region):
      - Rare malignant cells
      - Slight inflammatory change.

records.query: Need the liver biopsy immunohistochemistry panel details (e.g., CK7, CK20, TTF-1, PAX8 distribution) and a PET-CT to identify the primary site of the PAX8-positive metastatic carcinoma, as this is essential to confirm the hilar biliary obstruction is due to metastasis and to guide further management.

bindings.label: A 27-year-old woman presented with elevated hepatobiliary enzymes
The patient occasionally drank alcohol and was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride
The patient had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease
After stopping alcohol and axitinib, the patient's hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged
Physical examination showed no specific findings
Laboratory tests show markedly elevated ALP of 1028 U/L
Laboratory tests show markedly elevated GGT of 257 U/L
Ultrasound shows an irregular isoechoic region at the hepatic hilum
Liver biopsy shows PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule with bile duct destruction
Metastatic carcinoma involving the hepatic hilum is causing the cholestatic liver injury
Transaminases are only mildly elevated compared with markedly elevated ALP and GGT
MRI shows hypointensity in the hepatic hilum region
